text: Release automation added in 2ab52e8. sbt-ci-release 1.12.1 publishes signed artifacts to the Sonatype Central Portal from .github/workflows/release.yml, which runs only on a v* tag or a manual dispatch -- there is no snapshot-on-merge step, so no accidental artifact can reach Central. build.sbt no longer sets version: sbt-dynver derives it from the git state, so a tag is the only thing that names a release. The job sets CI_RELEASE=publishSigned rather than the plugin's default +publishSigned, because both Scala lines produce the same _3 coordinates and cross-publishing would overwrite the LTS build. Policies: CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog, with an explicit Breaking list), MIGRATION.md (each break with its compiler error and the edit that fixes it), CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md (private advisory reporting, with output injection, untrusted compiler input and renderer resource exhaustion named as in scope), and docs/releasing.md; docs/compatibility.md already existed and gained a section on the baseline being compiler-bound. The clean-clone rehearsal is tools/release-rehearsal.sh, run as a job that must pass before the publishing job starts: it clones HEAD into a scratch directory, builds with its own user.home, ivy home, coursier cache and sbt boot directory so a stale local artifact cannot substitute for a missing dependency, publishes every module to a throwaway local Maven repository, then reads the POM closure back and checks that each of the eleven publishable modules produced a POM, jar and sources jar; that each POM carries name, description, url, licenses, developers and scm; that nothing in the closure depends on a SNAPSHOT; that every third-party coordinate resolves from Maven Central; and that the three publish/skip modules stayed unpublished. Nothing is signed and nothing is uploaded. Evidence: the rehearsal passes on main -- eleven modules, complete metadata, nine third-party coordinates all resolvable, no skipped module published. Two courts were corrected by using them: tools/check-compatibility.sh now writes a version.sbt into its export (an archive has no history for sbt-dynver) and derives the candidate version from baseline.conf instead of hard-coding 0.1.1-SNAPSHOT, which silently assumed a 0.1.0 baseline. Not established: the workflow has never run. No tag exists, no credentials are configured, and nothing has been published, so the rehearsal proves the artifacts are well-formed, not that the upload path works. Twice, when the rehearsal ran immediately after two other sbt invocations in one shell, scaladoc died with an NPE in MemberRenderer; it did not reproduce in four standalone runs, including a clean clone with the same isolation flags. The release workflow runs the rehearsal as its own job on a fresh runner, so the exposure is low, but it is unexplained.
